text: DATA MANAGEMENT PLAN

label: section
text: REVIEW OF PROPOSAL COMPONENTS

label: content
text: The proposal is separated into three sections.

label: content
text: Section 2.1 characterizes the aquifer formation that each groundwater well in the West taps and

label: content
text: compares well construction patterns before and after the establishment of regulatory controls.

label: content
text: • Section 2.2 estimates groundwater components of the water budget (withdrawals and consumption)

label: content
text: yearly (2016-2021) at the field scale.

label: content
text: • Section 2.3 integrates research and education through the Scientist Spotlight and Hydrologic

label: content
text: Sciences Workshops.

label: section
text: TYPES OF DATA

label: content
text: The PI and PhD student will be responsible for all data-related activities including: collection, documentation and metadata description, quality control, storage and backup, archiving, and sharing.

label: content
text: Input data: Available data will be systematically reviewed and downloaded. These data are likely

label: content
text: available in the form of Microsoft Access files or Microsoft Excel spreadsheets; shapefiles or raster files;

label: content
text: Produced Data: Datasets will be produced in Sections 2.1-2.3 of the proposal. These datasets will be

label: content
text: formatted and shared in an open format (e.g., CSV) or in illustrator files (i.e., cross sections).

label: section
text: DATA AND METADATA STANDARDS

label: content
text: The data will be shared along with a README.txt, which will describe all files, their relationships,

label: content
text: • Scripts and code for analyses: All scripts and code will be archived in supplementary information

label: content
text: appendices in publications as well as uploaded to Zenodo through the Dryad repository submission process along with the sharable raw and processed data in order to allow citations and a better connection to the research data curation and publication processes.

label: section
text: Scientist spotlight: All scientist spotlight biographies, assignments, and open-access readings will be

label: content
text: posted to an online Dashboard associated with the PI’s website, which is updated bi-monthly.

label: subsection
text: Workshop frameworks: Workshop material will be shared with UCSB’s Diversity Committee through

label: content
text: Google Drive; if workshop materials are fully supported by the Diversity Committee, these materials will also be shared through eSholarship for broader dissemination.

label: section
text: POLICIES FOR ACCESS AND SHARING

label: content
text: Raw data: Detailed information about how the data were obtained, including detailed contact information or websites for direct download and citations to all datasets will be provided to allow for accessibility and correct attribution to original collectors.

label: content
text: Scripts and code for analyses: All scripts and code will be archived in supplementary information

label: content
text: appendices in publications as well as uploaded to Zenodo through the Dryad repository submission process along with the sharable raw and processed data in order to allow citations and a better connection to the research data curation and publication processes.

label: section
text: POLICIES AND PROVISIONS FOR RE-USE, RE-DISTRIBUTION

label: content
text: All data deposited at Dryad will be publicly available under a CC0 license, meaning that others may freely build upon, enhance and reuse the works for any purposes without restriction under copyright or database law.

label: section
text: PLANS FOR ARCHIVING AND PRESERVATION OF ACCESS

label: content
text: UCSB Box will be used as the primary means to store and back up all collected input, generated output data sets and code, and educational materials over the course of the project and prior to data sharing.
